newsitem.title: JAPAN: Takuma wins 36 bln yen order for incinerator plant.
newsitem.headline: Takuma wins 36 bln yen order for incinerator plant.

text.p: Incinerator maker Takuma Co Ltd said on Tuesday it had won a 36.28 billion yen contract for a garbage incinerator plant from the city of Sapporo, northern Japan.
The plant will include three incinerators, each with a disposal capacity of 300 tonnes per day, Takuma said.
The volume of dioxin emissions from the new plant will be less than that of conventional incinerating plants, the company said.
Construction of the plant is expected to begin in spring 1998 and end in November 2002, Takuma said in a statement.
The plant will be partly subsidised by the central government, it added.

Brokers said speculative buying of shares in environment-related companies had recently been fuelled by expectations that an Environment Agency committee would decide later this month to recommend controls on dioxin emissions from industrial incinerators.
Dioxin is a highly toxic by-product of some industrial processes and is known to cause a wide range of diseases, including cancer.
